courseTitle: Ancient Greece — City-States, Myths & Legacy (c. 800–146 BC)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: Ancient Greece
root.gloss: How mountain-divided Greek city-states invented democracy, staged the 776 BC Olympics, defeated Persia, and shaped modern theatre, science, and words.

children.label: 1. Poleis: Athens & Sparta
children.gloss: Mountains and islands split Greece into rival city-states sharing one alphabet, with sea-trading democratic Athens contrasting sharply against warrior Sparta.

children.label: 1. Mountains & Rival City-States
children.q2Chain: Mountains & islands split rival poleis → Every polis builds Acropolis & Agora → 24-letter alphabet & olive-oil sea trade unite Hellenes
children.gloss: Mountains & islands split rival poleis → Every polis builds Acropolis & Agora → 24-letter alphabet & olive-oil sea trade unite Hellenes

children.label: Mountains & Islands Split Poleis
children.gloss: After Minoans and Mycenaeans, steep mountains and a thousand Aegean islands divided Greeks into rival city-states called poleis.

children.label: Steep Peaks & 1,000+ Islands
children.gloss: Minoans and Mycenaeans came first; Slow mountain tracks split valleys.

children.label: Rival Poleis Kept Own Laws
children.gloss: Athens, Sparta, Corinth, and Thebes; Minted separate city-state coins.

children.label: → Each Polis Built Two Spaces
children.gloss: Stopped Greece becoming one kingdom; Needed hilltop fort and market.

children.label: High Acropolis & Busy Agora
children.gloss: Almost every Greek city-state crowned a walled hill called the Acropolis with marble temples above a sunny Agora marketplace.

children.label: Walled Acropolis Held Temples
children.gloss: Sheltered families during enemy raids; Honoured city’s chosen patron god.

children.label: Sunny Agora for Stalls & Debate
children.gloss: Sold figs, goat cheese, fish; Men debated morning city laws.

children.label: → Connected Sailors & Markets
children.gloss: Potters stacked painted clay bowls; Spread shared ideas across ports.

children.label: 24 Letters, Olives & Sea Trade
children.gloss: Proud Greeks called themselves Hellenes, adapted a 24-letter alphabet with vowels, and traded olive oil and pottery for wheat.

children.label: One Hellene Speech & 24 Letters
children.gloss: Adapted Phoenician signs c. 800 BC; Added vowels for stone laws.

children.label: Ships Traded Olive Oil for Wheat
children.gloss: Thin rocky soil grew olives; Exported painted jars across seas.

children.label: United Rival Greeks by Culture
children.gloss: Shared language and Olympian gods; Allowed rival cities distinct rules.

children.label: 2. Growing Up: Athens & Sparta
children.q2Chain: Athenian male citizens vote on Pnyx (c. 508 BC) → Spartan boys enter agoge barracks at seven → Contrasting lives for girls & women
children.gloss: Athenian male citizens vote on Pnyx (c. 508 BC) → Spartan boys enter agoge barracks at seven → Contrasting lives for girls & women

children.label: People-Power on Athens’s Pnyx
children.gloss: Around 508 BC, Athens invented direct democracy on the Pnyx hill, though women, enslaved people, and foreign metics were shut out.

children.label: Pnyx Hand Votes & Ostrakon Shards
children.gloss: Male citizens voted every law; Scratched pottery shards banished bosses.

children.label: 500 Jurors Picked by Machine
children.gloss: Marble kleroterion dropped chance balls; Shut out women, enslaved, metics.

children.label: → Clashed With Warrior Sparta
children.gloss: Invented people-power c. 508 BC; Inland Sparta prized strict obedience.

children.label: Two Kings & Agoge Barracks
children.gloss: Ruled by two kings while helots farmed, Sparta took boys aged seven into harsh agoge barracks to train barefoot full-time.

children.label: Two Kings & Helot Farmworkers
children.gloss: Council of older nobles advised; Helots grew crops for soldiers.

children.label: Age Seven Into Barefoot Agoge
children.gloss: Slept on winter river reeds; Ate dark broth; practised stealth.

children.label: → Shaped Girls & Women Differently
children.gloss: Forged Greece’s toughest land army; Left Spartan wives running farms.

children.label: Athenian vs Spartan Childhoods
children.gloss: Athenian boys studied books while girls stayed indoors; Spartan girls wrestled outdoors and Spartan women owned land!

children.label: Athenian Tutors vs Indoor Looms
children.gloss: Boys learned reading, music, geometry; Girls learned spinning indoors.

children.label: Spartan Girls Ran & Owned Land
children.gloss: Ran, wrestled, threw javelins outdoors; Spartan women owned farm land.

children.label: Two Opposite Greek Ways of Life
children.gloss: Spoke openly in public streets; Yet shared gods united both.

children.label: 2. Gods, Olympics & Persia
children.gloss: Shared worship of Mount Olympus’s twelve gods and the 776 BC Olympic Truce brought rival Greeks together before Persia invaded at Marathon, Thermopylae, and Salamis.

children.label: 3. Gods, Myths & 776 BC Olympics
children.q2Chain: Twelve Olympian gods & Parthenon temples → Delphi’s Oracle & vase myths → Sacred Truce & 776 BC Olympic olive crowns
children.gloss: Twelve Olympian gods & Parthenon temples → Delphi’s Oracle & vase myths → Sacred Truce & 776 BC Olympic olive crowns

children.label: Twelve Gods & Marble Temples
children.gloss: Believing twelve gods ruled snowy Mount Olympus, cities built marble homes like Athens’s Parthenon and worshipped at smoky altars.

children.label: Zeus, Hera, Poseidon & Athena
children.gloss: Zeus hurled thunderbolts on Olympus; Twins Apollo, Artemis; winged Hermes.

children.label: Parthenon Statue & Outdoor Altars
children.gloss: Gold-and-ivory Athena stood inside; Poured wine, roasted meat outdoors.

children.label: → Inspired Oracles & Hero Myths
children.gloss: Sweet smoke rose toward sky; Shaped Greek art and stories.

children.label: Delphi’s Oracle & Painted Vases
children.gloss: Generals climbed Delphi to question Apollo’s Pythia priestess, while potters painted Heracles, Odysseus, and Medusa on clay vases.

children.label: Pythia Spoke Riddles at Delphi
children.gloss: Leaders asked before wars, voyages; Studied Apollo’s riddles before wars.

children.label: Heroes & Monsters on Clay Vases
children.gloss: Heracles fought Hydra; Perseus Medusa; Painted black- and red-figure vases.

children.label: → Shared Faith Drew Olympia Crowds
children.gloss: Turned supper jars into storybooks; United cities in Zeus’s games.

children.label: 776 BC Olympia & Olive Crowns
children.gloss: Every four summers from 776 BC, the Sacred Truce paused wars so athletes raced at Olympia for wild-olive kotinos crowns.

children.label: Sacred Truce Paused City Wars
children.gloss: Messengers announced Ekecheiria peace; Crowds travelled safely to Olympia.

children.label: Barefoot Sprints, Chariots & Olive
children.gloss: Barefoot sprints, discus, fast chariots; Winners wore wild-olive kotinos crowns.

children.label: Proved Rival Greeks Could Unite
children.gloss: Swore beside Zeus’s smoky altar; Practised unity before Persian wars.

children.label: 4. Persian Wars (490–479 BC)
children.q2Chain: Hoplite phalanx wins at Marathon (490 BC) → 300 Spartans hold narrow Thermopylae (480 BC) → Triremes ram Xerxes’s fleet at Salamis
children.gloss: Hoplite phalanx wins at Marathon (490 BC) → 300 Spartans hold narrow Thermopylae (480 BC) → Triremes ram Xerxes’s fleet at Salamis

children.label: 490 BC: Phalanx Wins at Marathon
children.gloss: When Persian King Darius I landed troops at Marathon in 490 BC, Athenian hoplites charged in a tight bronze phalanx and won.

children.label: Darius Punished Athens for Rebels
children.gloss: Persian archers landed at Marathon; Citizen hoplites locked bronze shields.

children.label: Phalanx Charge & 26-Mile Run
children.gloss: Smashed straight through Persian lines; Pheidippides ran twenty-six miles home.

children.label: → King Xerxes Planned Huge Return
children.gloss: Inspired modern marathon foot race; Ten years later Xerxes marched.

children.label: 480 BC: Leonidas at Thermopylae
children.gloss: In 480 BC, Spartan King Leonidas and 300 Spartans blocked Xerxes’s vast army for three days inside narrow coastal Thermopylae.

children.label: Xerxes & Immortals Marched South
children.gloss: Rival Greeks united to defend; Guarded narrow pass by cliffs.

children.label: 300 Spartans Held Pass 3 Days
children.gloss: Blocked thousands of Persian troops; Traitor showed secret mountain path.

children.label: → Bought Time to Evacuate Athens
children.gloss: Leonidas stayed so allies escaped; Families sailed safe before Salamis.

children.label: 480 BC: Triremes Win at Salamis
children.gloss: Admiral Themistocles lured Xerxes’s fleet into the narrow Strait of Salamis, where 170-oar wooden triremes rammed jammed ships.

children.label: 170-Oar Triremes With Bronze Rams
children.gloss: Three levels of wooden oars; Painted eyes gleamed above waterline.

children.label: Trick Message Trapped Xerxes’s Ships
children.gloss: Jammed inside narrow Salamis strait; Nimble Greek hulls rammed Persians.

children.label: → Saved Free Greece for Golden Age
children.gloss: Won Salamis 480, Plataea 479; Sparked Athens’s golden drama age.

children.label: 3. Ideas, Alexander & Legacy
children.gloss: Free Greek cities pioneered hillside drama, philosophy, clinical medicine, and geometry, spread across three continents by Alexander and living on today.

children.label: 5. Theatre, Philosophy & Science
children.q2Chain: 14,000 watch masked plays at Epidaurus → Socrates, Plato & Aristotle question & classify → Hippocrates & Greek geometry transform science
children.gloss: 14,000 watch masked plays at Epidaurus → Socrates, Plato & Aristotle question & classify → Hippocrates & Greek geometry transform science

children.label: Epidaurus Theatre & Bold Masks
children.gloss: Curved hillside stone theatres like Epidaurus seated 14,000 spectators to watch masked tragedies and comedies for Dionysus.

children.label: 14,000 Seats Carried Every Whisper
children.gloss: Carved curved stone into hillsides; Staged plays at Dionysus festivals.

children.label: Wide Masks, Tragedies & Comedies
children.gloss: Distant rows saw bold faces; Poor citizens received coin tokens.

children.label: → Sparked Public Debate on Justice
children.gloss: Crowds debated pride and fairness; Prepared Athens for bold thinkers.

children.label: Socrates, Plato & Aristotle
children.gloss: Barefoot Socrates questioned citizens in the Agora, Plato opened the Academy, and Aristotle observed and sorted living nature.

children.label: Socrates Questioned Every Belief
children.gloss: Walked barefoot through daily Agora; Drank poison in 399 BC.

children.label: Plato’s Academy & Aristotle’s Facts
children.gloss: Plato taught inside shady Academy; Aristotle grouped plants at Lyceum.

children.label: → Inspired Real Medical Evidence
children.gloss: Measured real facts over myths; Built lasting roots for science.

children.label: Hippocrates, Euclid & Archimedes
children.gloss: Hippocrates checked natural symptoms on Kos, while Pythagoras, Euclid, and Archimedes unlocked triangles, geometry, and levers.

children.label: Hippocrates Checked Bedside Notes
children.gloss: Prescribed clean food, fresh air; Doctors swore ethical Hippocratic Oath.

children.label: Triangles, Geometry & “Eureka!”
children.gloss: Pythagoras triangles; Euclid’s geometry; Archimedes solved bath lever puzzle.

children.label: → Aristotle Taught Young Alexander
children.gloss: Replaced magic cures with symptoms; Ready to spread across continents.

children.label: 6. Alexander & Greek Legacy
children.q2Chain: Alexander & Bucephalus build 3-continent empire (336–323 BC) → Alexandria’s Library & Rome (146 BC) → Democracy, words & 1896 Olympics
children.gloss: Alexander & Bucephalus build 3-continent empire (336–323 BC) → Alexandria’s Library & Rome (146 BC) → Democracy, words & 1896 Olympics

children.label: Alexander & Horse Bucephalus
children.gloss: Taught by Aristotle, young Macedonian King Alexander tamed Bucephalus and marched unbeaten across Egypt, Persia, and north-west India.

children.label: Taught by Aristotle in Macedon
children.gloss: Tamed wild black warhorse Bucephalus; Crowned king aged twenty, 336 BC.

children.label: Unbeaten March to North-West India
children.gloss: Led armies eleven straight years; Founded Greek cities named Alexandria.

children.label: → Shaped Lively Hellenistic World
children.gloss: Blended Greek and eastern customs; Sparked Alexandria’s famous port library.

children.label: Great Library & Conquering Rome
children.gloss: Alexandria’s Pharos Lighthouse and Great Library shone with Greek scrolls, dazzling the Roman Republic even after Rome conquered Greece in 146 BC.

children.label: Pharos Tower & Scroll Library
children.gloss: Gathered hundreds of thousands scrolls; Scholars studied stars and Euclid.

children.label: Rome Conquered Yet Copied Greece
children.gloss: Roman legions took Greece 146 BC; Hired Greek teachers, copied statues.

children.label: → Carried Greek Ideas Across Europe
children.gloss: Educated Romans read poet Homer; Passed Greek learning toward Britain.

children.label: Votes, Words, Columns & 1896
children.gloss: Elections, juries, Greek words, stone columns, and the 1896 Athens Modern Olympics prove Greece’s legacy still shapes daily life.

children.label: Votes, Juries & Everyday Words
children.gloss: Echoes Athenian voting and juries; Words: school, dinosaur, planet, music.

children.label: Stone Columns & 1896 Olympics
children.gloss: Doric, Ionic, leafy Corinthian columns; 1896 Panathenaic Stadium launched Games.

children.label: Shaped Modern Classrooms & Sport
children.gloss: Fourteen nations raced in 1896; Tiny poleis left lasting footprint.
